newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea facility investment seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea facility investment seen slowing.

text.p: Facilities investment by South Korean companies is forecast to grow 6.4 percent year-on-year this year, slowing from a 15.7 percent rise last year, state-run Korea Development Bank said on Tuesday.

The bank attributed the slowdown to a financial squeeze as domestic financial institutions have been more cautious in extending loans following the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co Ltd and Sammi Steel Co Ltd earlier this year.
Facilities investment by manufacturers is expected to slip 1.3 percent this year against a 15.8 percent rise a year earlier, the bank said.
But facilities investment in the non-manufacturing sector is seen rising 23.8 percent thanks to increasing investment in the fields of telecommunications, electricity and gas.

The bank said domestic companies showed strong interest in a burgeoning high-tech industry including non-memory chips, thin film transistor liquid crystal displays (TFT-LCD) and mobile telecommunications.
